cand.title: Inaugural 2026 WNBA season
cand.excerpt: Toronto’s first WNBA team launched an inaugural season with home games primarily at Coca-Cola Coliseum and selected games at Scotiabank Arena; visiting WNBA teams, league personnel, media and sponsors create a recurring sports-event lodging opportunity.
linkedLedgerProgrammes: Toronto Tempo / WNBA — Inaugural 2026 WNBA season

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Lisa Ferkul, Chief Revenue Officer, is directly quoted in the Hotel X partnership announcement: verified commercial lead, not a verified travel-contract signatory. Amy Williams, Director, Partnerships, is a second commercially relevant lead verified through her professional profile. Teresa Resch, President, is an executive relationship/escalation lead. None is proven to control visiting-team or league hotel procurement. Bri Bijman is a published team-information contact, suitable for routing only; her precise title and lodging remit are not established by the cited release.
findings.futureEdition: 2026 is past and outside the December 2026–June 2028 prospecting horizon. The next indicated cycle is 2027: official Ticket Central says '2027 Single-Game Tickets Coming Soon'; the Cross-Canada Series page says 'Will be back in 2027' and 'Stay tuned for more information when the schedule is released.' No officially published 2027 or 2028 game dates were located. Upcoming start/end dates and game-specific city/venue assignments remain null; do not roll 2026 dates forward or promise games before June 2028.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel specification: a 157-room Harbourfront city hotel is plausible for limited fan, media, sponsor or executive lodging and separately qualified small groups, not exclusive housing for the event audience. The supplied approximately 15–109 peak-room target is a sales-fit range, NOT event demand evidence. Arena games stay at the arenas; the Admiral Ballroom is only a possible small ancillary-meeting venue, not a substitute sports venue. Resort amenities are not a published event requirement. Hotel X has an Exhibition Place proximity advantage; Radisson should sell a distinct downtown/Harbourfront lodging alternative, not assumed sports-team suitability. Player/team bids require verification of privacy, transport, meals and service standards; restaurant/lounge and catering availability remain unverified.
findings.venueCommitments: Historical 2026: primary home venue Coca-Cola Coliseum, Exhibition Place, Toronto proper. Scotiabank Arena, 40 Bay Street, downtown Toronto proper, hosted June 27 (Phoenix), July 30 (Minnesota), and August 18 (Indiana). Bell Centre, Montreal, hosted July 10 and 12; Rogers Arena, Vancouver, hosted August 21 and 23: these are outside the hotel's Toronto territory. These are arena commitments, not hotel commitments. No game-specific 2027 venue assignment or future arena-contract term was verified.
findings.historicalRotation: 2026 was the inaugural season, not a rotating association convention. The league announced 44 games per team, including 22 home games. Toronto home activity began May 8 at Coca-Cola Coliseum; its home finale was September 20 there. The league regular-season calendar was May 8–September 24. Montreal and Vancouver were additional 2026 home markets, not prior annual host editions. One inaugural season does not establish a multi-year destination rotation.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Documented incumbent: Hotel X Toronto only. The May 6, 2026 joint announcement calls it the team's 'official domestic hotel partner' and says: 'Hotel X Toronto will offer exclusive rates to Toronto Tempo fans staying at the hotel on home game days with a valid ticket'. Its game-day offer publishes 15% off and self-parking included. This establishes a Tempo-specific fan lodging partnership, not a quantified room block or proof that players, visiting teams, league personnel, officials, media or sponsors stay there. No official housing bureau, open lodging RFP, room-block allocation, travel-management company or additional team-contracted hotel was located. Sourcing for those non-fan segments remains unknown. 'Exclusive rates' must not be read as exclusive control of all event accommodation; contract term and category restrictions are undisclosed.
findings.organizationStructure: Corporate professional-sports franchise, not an association conference. WNBA is the league; Toronto Tempo is the franchise/programme operator. Official WNBA material identifies Kilmer Sports Ventures as owner/operator, and a July 2026 release describes the team as controlled by Kilmer Sports Ventures with an expanded ownership group. Coca-Cola Coliseum and the other arenas are venues; Hotel X is the documented domestic hotel partner. No PCO, DMC or housing agency was identified.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Hotel X already holds a documented domestic-partner position and a game-day fan offer. Its release reports 404 rooms/suites and 60,000 sq ft of event space; its offer stresses proximity to Coca-Cola Coliseum. Those are real competitive limitations, not evidence that all lodging is committed. Neither sold-out hotel inventory, an overflow referral agreement, displaced room nights nor unmet hotel demand was evidenced. Arena sellouts and crowd totals do not establish hotel compression. Exclusivity, renewal date and rights to independent fan or sponsor bookings require confirmation.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Lisa Ferkul and Amy Williams with a concise accommodation-capability introduction, explicitly acknowledging Hotel X's incumbent domestic partnership. Ask whether any non-exclusive lodging segments or future supplier reviews are accessible, who sources basketball/team travel versus commercial guest travel, and when hotel rights are reviewed. Use Teresa Resch only for strategic escalation; the published Bri Bijman team-information channel can route an inquiry, not serve as a presumed procurement desk. Request the 2027 Toronto schedule when available, buyer-approved rooming requirements, dates, peak rooms, room nights and rate/RFP process before quoting. Verify hotel food-service capability before offering meals or receptions. Do not represent this lead as SALES_READY without those answers.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: No remaining 2026 home-game opportunity: the official September 20 game page identifies the home finale. Hotel X's historical partnership does not prove open or closed 2027 inventory. No date-specific, bookable or openly tendered opportunity for Radisson was verified within the requested horizon. Treat this as relationship development, not an active room-block lead.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: cultivate a secondary, non-conflicting lodging relationship for future Toronto fixtures, with independent fan groups or separately procured sponsor/media/executive stays as hypotheses. Do not assume access to visiting-team lodging, an overflow need, Hotel X displacement or 2027 Scotiabank games. Reassess after the official schedule identifies Toronto fixtures and after the partner's rights and renewal cycle are clarified; exclude Montreal/Vancouver games from Toronto room-demand projections.
